Hibernian arrived at Celtic Park shortly after manager John Collins unexpectedly stepped down on Thursday, saying he had not received enough financial backing from the Edinburgh club’s board. Despite that disruption, the visitors went in front after 20 minutes through left-back Murphy.

The English defender exchanged passes with Abdessalam Benjelloun, then struck a powerful effort from the edge of the penalty area that beat goalkeeper Mark Brown, hit the underside of the crossbar and went in. Murphy’s only previous goal of the campaign had come in Hibs’ 1-0 victory away to Rangers on October 6.

Brown later produced a strong save to deny Merouane Zemmama’s ambitious attempt from just inside the Celtic half, and three minutes after the interval he also tipped Brian Kerr’s looping header over the bar.

Celtic avoided what would have been their first home SPL defeat of the season when substitute Jiri Jarosik equalized in the 78th minute. Jan Vennegoor of Hesselink set him up, and the Dutch striker then came close to winning it when he headed against the post with two minutes remaining.

Hibernian managed to preserve the draw even though they finished the match with 10 players, after Benjelloun was carried off on a stretcher once all three substitutions had already been made.

The result moved Hibernian up to fifth place, while Celtic have now earned only six points from their last five league matches.

Strachan, who said he hopes to bring in Brazilian defender Coelho next month, admitted Celtic must stop gifting opponents chances.

“We need to cut out the silly mistakes because if you look at some of the goals we have let in away from home this season, they are silly mistakes,” he said.

“We could have definitely done something with every one of them. I’m happy with the number of chances we’ve made in the last few weeks, but unhappy with individual mistakes.

“It’s not been great to look at, and we need to cut it out. We have honest lads walking into the dressing room and saying, ‘That was my fault.’

“I said to them, ‘It’s very commendable lads but we can’t keep doing this.’ There has been a lot going right for us, but one or two things going wrong. We have to deal with that, and then I will look forward to the rest of the season.”

Fourth-place Dundee United also missed the chance to capitalize, losing 2-1 at home to bottom side Gretna. Gretna’s only two victories of the season have both come against United. Kenny Deuchar gave the visitors the lead in the 12th minute, Noel Hunt equalized in the 29th, and Nicky Deverdics scored what proved to be the winning goal for the Borders club three minutes before half-time.
